description: Solar-X is built by a passionate, multidisciplinary team dedicated to transforming complex aerospace engineering into an accessible, engaging, and educational experience. Combining our expertise in systems design, creative UI/UX, software development, and space science, we bridge the gap between abstract orbital mechanics and practical gameplay.
summary: Solar-X transforms the complex reality of aerospace systems engineering into an immersive 2D & 3D simulation game. It addresses the challenge by allowing players to design, balance, and fly real NASA-grounded spacecraft, but it goes further: it turns abstract trade-offs into tangible consequences by managing coupled mass, power, RF links, orbits, and budgets through NASA JPL's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4). Its true importance lies in being more than a CAD tool; it is a rigorous flight-readiness simulator that tests designs against real operational anomalies, proving whether an envisioned mission can actually survive launch and orbit.
details:
Overview Solar-X: Space Mission Architect solves Challenge 13 (Space Mission Design Game) by transforming the real engineering lifecycle of space missions (NASA JPL Concept Maturity Levels – CML 1 to 4) into an interactive, visual, and physics-driven simulation. It features 5 difficulty tiers (Explorer/Beginner, Discovery/Intermediate, New Frontiers/Advanced, Flagship/Expert, and Open Lab/Sandbox) and supports both Solo or 4-Player Crew modes with distinct engineering roles (Principal Investigator, Spacecraft Systems Engineer, Flight Dynamics & Launch Lead, and Mission Ops & Comms Lead).

Key Features Implemented

Interactive Landing Page: Clean introduction featuring a live 3D planet and satellite, a 4-stage interactive workflow preview, a real-time coupled trade-off mini-lab, and quick control guides.

CML 1–4 Design Workbench (2D + 3D):

  • CML 1 (Objectives): Science Traceability Matrix (STM) goals and margin rigor definition.
  • CML 2 (Bus & Power): Structure selection (3U/6U/12U CubeSats up to ESPA, Discovery, and Flagship buses), solar arrays (affected by inverse-square solar attenuation), batteries (UL-1642 compliance and eclipse depth of discharge), avionics/ADCS, and thermal materials.
  • CML 3 (Science): Instrument selection with real constraints on mass, power, data rate, arc-second pointing, and physical envelope (mm protrusion).
  • CML 4 (Orbit & Ops): Orbit selection (LEO, SSO, Lunar NRHO, Mars, Europa), launch vehicle, communication bands (UHF, S-Band, X-Band, Ka-Band, Optical), ground station networks, and environmental testing/licenses (DITL, Vibration, TVAC, FCC, NOAA, ODAR).

Coupled Physics & Structural Failure Alerts: All decisions are interdependent. Heavy instruments require larger buses and rockets, increasing mass and cost; distant orbits reduce solar power ($1/r^2$) and demand high-gain antennas/Deep Space Network support. If any margin fails, the launch gate triggers a detailed Structural Engineering Failure Alert.

3D & 2D Visualizations + Multiplatform Controls:

  • 3D View (Three.js): Procedural spacecraft model (including Exploded CAD view), multi-stage rocket with retractable launch pad, continuous curved trajectory crossing the 100 km Kármán line, stage separation, fairing ejection, satellite release, and solar array deployment.
  • 2D View: Equirectangular ground-track map with ground stations and a Trade-Space Radar telemetry dashboard.
  • Controls: Full support for keyboard, mouse (direct 3D orbital node dragging), and PS4 (DualShock 4) / PS5 (DualSense) controllers via Gamepad API with haptics.

Flight Simulation & Post-Flight Review (TMCO): Real-time mission execution featuring eclipses, ground station passes, randomized in-flight anomalies with team-role decisions, and a formal post-flight assessment score (CML Readiness, Resource Efficiency, and Science Return).
